items.headline: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
items.blurb: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.
items.text: The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders. Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said. Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin. Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole. items.headline: Arab parties projected to win 18 seats in Israeli parliamentary election
items.blurb: Record-breaking voter turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel hits around 80 percent, early indications show.
items.text: Israel’s Arab parties are projected to win 18 seats in the Israeli parliament, exit polls indicate, after voting among Palestinian citizens of Israel surged to their highest levels in decades. Exit polling data from Tuesday’s vote suggested that the leading Arab-led parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, are set to hold a record number of seats in the 120-member Knesset. Updated exit polling indicated that the opposition bloc led by former Israeli military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party and the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party were tied at 51 seats each. Early indications put voter turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel at around 80 percent, historic numbers that break 1999 records, Israel’s Channel 12 reported on Tuesday. The leader of Ra’am, or the United Arab List, Mansour Abbas, said he hopes the final election results will allow the anti-Netanyahu bloc, including his party, to win the 61 seats required to form a government. “With the numbers we have now, there is no government,” Abbas told Israel’s Channel 12. items.text: Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days. A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city. A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze . The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”. items.headline: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
items.blurb: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.
items.text: A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources. Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity. On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous. However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported. US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys. That was later corroborated by the press secretary to Ukraine's public ombudsman, and by Oleksandr Tolokonnikov, deputy head of Kherson, who said Russian shelling had stopped both in Kherson city, which is in Ukrainian hands, and the wider region. items.headline: Netanyahu, Eisenkot camps clash over Israeli election projections
items.blurb: Despite narrower exit poll figures, opposition leaders insisted the result was a defeat for the government.
items.text: Israeli political leaders have traded sharp reactions to exit poll projections showing no clear winner between the country’s main political blocs. Updated figures broadcast by Israel’s Channel 13 showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led coalition tied at 51 seats with the opposition bloc led by challenger Gadi Eisenkot in the 120-seat Knesset. Despite narrower exit poll figures, opposition leaders insisted the result was a defeat for the government. Eisenkot, head of the Yashar party and a former military chief of staff, told supporters after voting closed that the initial projections showed a “complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government”, according to the AFP news agency. “Don’t let anyone confuse you: the Netanyahu bloc has suffered a crushing defeat,” opposition leader Yair Lapid said in a statement. “This is a total collapse and the public has told them to go home.” Under the updated figures, unaligned Arab parties were expected to hold 18 seats, leaving both major camps 10 seats short of the 61 required for an absolute majority. items.text: Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety. Is it a deliberate military strategy? T he water was rising rapidly. It had already reached Cayni Ali’s waist. Her home, five metres from the flooded River Juba in southern Somalia , never stood a chance. There was nowhere to go. Ali’s city of Jilib was under attack. Repeated airstrikes, said the mother of six, were pinning its population beside the rising river. “The drones come all the time,” said the 27-year-old. “We hear them constantly. They kill animals, civilians. The town is big but destruction is everywhere.” Asho Omar from Malenda, a village near Jilib, described “constant” airstrikes that had forced people towards the banks of the Juba. “The airstrikes are everywhere; it is difficult to move. So many people have been killed.” Their testimony offers a rare glimpse of life inside the stronghold of al-Shabaab , the Islamist militants who control 30% of Somalia. items.headline: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
items.blurb: The France star had referred to the former Chinese leader as a "dictator" during an interview about memes.
items.text: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands. Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao. The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement. Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans". items.headline: Sudan paramilitary drone strikes cause mass power cuts in eastern states
items.blurb: Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said.
items.text: Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said. The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref and one in White Nile state, “resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states”, the official said on condition of anonymity. All three states are controlled by the Sudanese army, which has been at war with the RSF, its former ally, since April 2023. The United Nations has repeatedly warned that regular attacks on power stations threaten health and services for millions of people who are already facing the world’s largest hunger crisis. Babiker Youssef, a resident of Al-Fao, in Gedaref, said the power had been out there since early morning. “My son is diabetic, his insulin has to be stored in the fridge,” he said over the phone, adding that he feared he would not be able to replace the medication

items.headline: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
items.blurb: The Trump-Lula relationship may have thawed, but several issues could reignite tensions between the two leaders.
items.text: "Brazil will not accept being anyone's backyard," Brazil's left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared in his election victory speech, a message squarely aimed at Washington. Domestic elections are rarely won on foreign policy, and this one was no different. But Lula's defiance against what he has described as US interference in Brazilian affairs evoked a patriotic spirit that proved an effective campaigning tool. It also chimed with his wider brand of politics as a former union leader: standing up to powerful figures. Paradoxically, it seems to have earned him President Donald Trump's respect. "I like Lula, we get along well," Trump said, responding to the result. "I didn't take sides," he added, before calling the election "terrible" and "rigged". If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival Flávio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. items.text: Severe cyclone Arnab made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast between Kakinada and Yanam of Puducherry early Wednesday affecting the entire coastal Andhra with destructive winds and torrential rains, disrupting normal life, authorities said. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the process of the extremely severe cyclone making landfall began on Tuesday night in Konaseema district and Narsapuram areas in West Godavari district. A bulletin released by AP State Disaster Management Authority chairman Prakhar Jain at 6am on Wednesday said the landfall process of the very severe cyclone Arnab was continuing, with its “eye” located approximately 30km from Narsapur, 55km from Yanam, 70km from Kakinada and 90km from Machilipatnam. “Gusty winds with speeds of 125–135 kmph have been reported in Kakinada, Konaseema and West Godavari districts and will continue over the next three hours,” Jain said. According to reports being received in the control room at the state secretariat, uprooted trees, fallen electricity poles, damaged roads, inundated low-lying areas and widespread power outages were reported from Srikakulam in the north to Bapatla in the south. items.headline: 18 months after Operation Sindoor, India invites Pakistan for SCO event in Delhi
items.blurb: All SCO members have been invited for the dialogue and the multilateral initiative has nothing to do with bilateral relations with Pakistan, officials said.
items.text: India has invited all 10 countries of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), including Pakistan, for the bloc’s inaugural Civilisational Dialogue Forum to be held in Delhi from November 20–22, officials aware of the matter said on Tuesday. Pakistan last attended the SCO’s foreign ministers’ meeting in Goa in May 2023. All SCO members have been invited for the dialogue and the multilateral initiative has nothing to do with bilateral relations with Pakistan, the officials said, adding that the development should be viewed in the broader context. Pakistan’s national heritage and culture minister Aurangzeb Khan Khichi has been invited, HT learns. Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed the dialogue at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year. External affairs minister S Jaishankar visited Pakistan in October 2024 for the SCO Council Heads of Government meeting, becoming the first Indian foreign minister to visit Pakistan in nine years. items.headline: Lab Rats series: A Pune biotech startup’s new approach to vitiligo cure
items.blurb: Ahammune has advanced its first-in-class drug to solve vitiligo to mid-trials with a fraction of the cost of global peers. It’s not been an easy road, but the tide is turning.
items.text: Mumbai: Every day, specialized cells in the skin produce melanin, the pigment that gives skin its colour. In people with vitiligo, a trigger can cause the cells to send out a distress signal. The immune system turns against these cells, destroying them and leaving behind patches of skin that lose their pigment. Existing cures involve suppressing the immune system or even targeting the distress signal pathway. The biggest piece of the puzzle is: what triggers the cell to release a distress signal in the first place? Pune-based Ahammune Biosciences believes the answer could lie in intervening before the immune system launches its attack. For chief executive Parul Ganju, an effective treatment must do more than halt the disease. It should stop the patches from spreading, restore pigmentation and ensure that the colour does not fade again. items.headline: Just Dial wants more paying merchants. Software is its next big bet
items.blurb: Just Dial, which currently generates most of its revenue from paid listings and subscriptions, is now testing new merchant software products to expand its offerings, its chief executive officer Dinkar Ayilavarapu said.
items.text: Just Dial Ltd, Reliance Group's business listings and search platform, plans to remain focused on helping consumers discover merchants rather than investing in order fulfilment infrastructure, as it looks to revamp its core offerings, a top company executive told Mint. "The products are in the lab right now, but they have already been tested with hundreds of merchants. And initial responses are awesome," he said. "This will come out into the world sooner rather than later." Ayilavarapu, a Bain & Co. veteran who joined Just Dial in July after leading Flipkart's strategy and then its business-to-business arm Flipkart Wholesale, said that the company is now focusing on increasing merchant count and average revenue per user (ARPU) by adding software tools alongside traditional paid search listings. While commerce platforms over the past five years have built out transaction capabilities, Ayilavarapu said his immediate priority is not to expand further into B2B commerce or business-to-consumer commerce marketplace models involving returns and logistics. Instead, Just Dial plans to centre operations around what he termed as 'Discovery plus plus.' Just Dial shares settled 1.4%

But remarkably, it was the hosts who booked their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-final thanks to their penalty shootout win over the Gunners. For the Cod Army, who won six promotions in 12 years in their impressive journey from non-league, this result will surely be remembered longest of all. Against the reigning Premier League champions, the club from a small seaside town in Lancashire created history in claiming one of the biggest cup upsets ever. Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts the lead after 21 minutes but, after the break, Viktor Gyokeres pulled the visitors level. items.text: A Delaware proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents would help the firms’ human owners evade legal responsibility for reckless and harmful actions taken by the AI, US Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) told Delaware Governor Matt Meyer in a letter yesterday. Comer, chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told Meyer that the committee “seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).” Comer said the proposal is ripe for abuse. “We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives,” Comer’s letter said. Comer suggested he may propose a federal law that would limit states’ regulatory authority. items.headline: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
items.blurb: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover.
items.text: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover. The machine settings matter, but so does knowing how a particular material behaves, what happened during the previous shift, and when an apparently minor variation deserves a closer look. A procedure can describe the sequence, but successful execution depends on the judgment that comes from experience and the organization’s accumulated know-how. That combination is industrial intelligence: a manufacturer’s accumulated know-how, operating practices, production data, and understanding of its own business. The opportunity now is to make more of that intelligence available wherever decisions are made, then connect it to the physical world of manufacturing. The strategic destination is not more agents, but rather to turn the existing business intelligence into an engine for profitable growth. Expertise has limited reach when it stays with one person, inside one system, or within one plant. The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wan to taper off her seizure medication and hide it from her doctors before she died in February, The New York Times reported . Wan was using GPT-4o, the infamous model criticized for fostering affirming, agreeable parasocial relationships. OpenAI, which had already announced its retirement, removed it from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after Wan died. The suit joins a line of cases against OpenAI that include the August 2025 lawsuit brought by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, which alleged OpenAI prioritized engagement over user safety . items.text: Marvel’s latest Disney Plus series is a reminder of how much a lot of gen AI hype is just science fiction.﻿ Marvel’s latest Disney Plus series is a reminder of how much a lot of gen AI hype is just science fiction.﻿ In Marvel’s VisionQuest , a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home. The series is deeply fantastical, yet it plays with some of the ideas that have come to dominate the conversation about real-world generative artificial intelligence, exploring whether we should look at thinking machines as people and if AI truly poses the kind of existential danger that should keep us up at night. It’s also a reminder how aggressively Silicon Valley has used the trappings of science fiction to sell us on its AI products. VisionQuest picks up some time after Agatha All Along and follows synthezoid Vision (Paul Bettany) on a journey of self-discovery. items.headline: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
items.blurb: You can apparently now tell AI tools what sort of protein you want them to make.
items.text: Protein design tools may be getting increasingly sophisticated , but you still need a sophisticated understanding of protein structure for them to work. This can include knowing enzyme mechanisms down to the positions of specific amino acids, as well as the water molecules that also occupy the area where catalysis takes place. Once you specify these, the tools can build the rest of a protein around this target. A large collaboration of researchers based in China, however, decided to bring protein design to the masses, making a tool that can take natural language prompts and use them to produce proteins with the function you specify. If your measure for success is a working protein, then the success rate may not be great. But they still manage to get the job done. And, in a separate announcement, Hugging Face shared that it’s now hosting a tool that does similar things on the DNA level. Mozilla is updating Smart Window — Firefox’s AI-powered browsing experience — with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs. As an example, Mozilla says Smart Window can pull information from your online portfolio or LinkedIn page to paste your work history into a job application. You can try out this feature by clicking into a form with at least four text fields. From there, you’ll see an option to “Fill from sources,” which will show all of the tabs Firefox will draw from. You can then select or deselect tabs that you want Firefox to use, and the browser will generate suggestions based on the information in them. items.headline: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
items.blurb: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide. A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl. These are important protections, and they should have existed all along.
items.text: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide . A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl . These are important protections, and they should have existed all along. But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships or trapped in feeds built to keep them scrolling. We have historically allowed the debate over technology to be defined by the worst thing a product might do, with remarkably little discussion of the insidious damage it does every day. As we transition into an era defined by powerful AI products, we should demand that the tech industry do more than merely address catastrophic harms. We should take measures to ensure that its products don’t erode how we think, learn, and interact with one another. Yet according to Anthropic’s S-1 , none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% of the company, according to recently reported Bloomberg figures.
